H_hierarchical.evidence: The controller is described as a flat sequential low-level, high-level, and both-switch flow; no parent mode, nested substate, or composite state is defined.

G_guards_arith.evidence: The transition logic depends on below-low-level, switch-1 active, switch-2 active, and a both-switch-active condition; the closing/buzzer branch is a boolean conjunction over two float-switch inputs.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Actions include green LED output, motor 1 forward to open gate 1, motor 2 forward to open gate 2, buzzer output, and both motors reversing to close both gates.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper mentions safety interlocks/buzzer behavior, but does not define a fault state, abort path, rollback, or recovery transition.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: The ladder-programming description already co-locates the main guards with the LED, motor, buzzer, and reverse-close actions; later gate-control and flowchart sections mainly restate the same behavior.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as float switch and low/high level are operationally explained in the paper; no unstated domain rule like fail-safe, manual override, or fault recovery must be decoded.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: There is no formal state/action table; the modeler must map narrated prose about LEDs, motors, gates, and buzzer behavior back onto EFSM transitions.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The both-level-switches-active case is a composed boolean guard over the lower and upper float-switch inputs.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite state exists, so there is no parent-state entry, during, or exit behavior beyond substates.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No from-any-state fault, emergency stop, or global safe-state transition is specified.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain is present.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The both-switch guard gives a weak expression-IR advantage, but the guards are otherwise simple threshold/input predicates.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: There is no cross-cutting transition over three or more substates and no parent-mode continuous monitor.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The outputs are concrete PLC effects: LED, buzzer, motors, and gates, not abstract notifications or publish/log actions.

key_nl_quotes: When both level switches turn on buzzer will turn on.
The PLC automatically opens or closes the dam gates
one_line_pitch: A compact PLC EFSM stress case where the core challenge is extracting boolean water-level guards and actuator actions from narrative ladder-logic prose.
rationale: This is a meaningful guard/action stress case: the controller has several threshold-driven transitions and a central both-switch branch that triggers buzzer and reverse-close actions. It lacks hierarchy and any explicit fault-recovery model, so it is not strong enough for the top candidate set. Its main value is as a compact backup sample for testing whether a method can recover EFSM guards and concrete transition outputs from prose.
